review_comments:
I am not sure how this handles the read error. It seems that errors are just (still) silently ignored now. 

If `uart_fifo_read` indeed can fail, then shouldn't we propagate that error and abort the read all-together?

No driver in the tree currently returns any errors. The only place that can happen is the common layer that abstracts the driver (drivers/uart.h) if a driver is missing an implementation. So it’s both a configuration error (incorrect or missing driver) and every call will create the same error. This is why I decided not to add new propagation of it higher up in the call stack.
Or to put it another way, this is really mostly a static analysis issue rather than something that would be seen in practice
I see. I'd like to see a `BT_WARN` or `BT_ERR` if `uart_fifo_read` returns `< 0` at least then.
@Thalley the PR has now been updated accordingly
